free_tier.stated: Free: Basic L3/L4 protection, 1 network, 1 TB traffic, Portless connection (Java), BungeeCord/Velocity support

egress.terms: 1 TB traffic on Free, 3 TB on Basic, 5 TB on Starter, 30 TB on Optimal, 150 TB on Professional; ingress: tcp
egress.free_allowance: 1 TB traffic on Free, 3 TB on Basic, 5 TB on Starter, 30 TB on Optimal, 150 TB on Professional

interface_detail: Panel and, from the Starter tier, REST API access.
tooling: DNS record in the panel, no client
chaining: Sits in front of a public origin as a DNS proxy; it does not give a private origin a public address.

limits.value: the free plan is 'Portless connection (Java)'; Bedrock tunnels appear only on Optimal (1 tunnel) and Professional (5 tunnels)

binding_note: The free plan's 1 TB is a real monthly byte counter and the vendor states the consequence: on exceeding the traffic limit the service is suspended within a few hours, after a warning that lets the customer buy more traffic or move up a plan.

identity_cost.detail: A panel account. The signup form was not opened and no page read names the required fields; payment on paid tiers runs through FreeKassa by card or SBP.

reliability_note: Exceeding the traffic limit suspends service within a few hours; traffic can be topped up or the plan raised.
confidence_note: Quota, Java-only free path and the suspension-on-overage sentence are all on the vendor's own English pricing page. The account fields would need a signup to establish.

evidence.proved: Free plan: 1 network, 3 domains, 1 TB traffic, Basic L3/L4, 'Portless connection (Java)'; Bedrock Edition support appears only from Optimal at RUB 2511/mo
The Russian page carries the same table plus the overage rule: on exceeding the traffic limit the service is suspended within a few hours
Front page states 1 TB of traffic free and describes Java and Bedrock protection as the product

notes: 1 TB is read as 10^12 bytes, which is 0.909 TiB; the page says TB throughout and never TiB. A genuine 1 TB/month free tier, the same headline number as TCPShield, but the free path is Java only and the Bedrock tunnel is a paid line item. Russian-facing product; the English pages are complete and were used so quotes stay ASCII.

extras.wg_detail: No WireGuard offering and no free UDP port.
extras.volume_stated: 1 TB traffic on Free, 3 TB on Basic, 5 TB on Starter, 30 TB on Optimal, 150 TB on Professional
extras.transit_note: MineGuard's filtering nodes proxy the game traffic
